title: HRSS: 111 people faced action over their views in 10 months
excerpt: Of the 111 people, 25 were journalists and 66 were arrested or detained. HRSS says cyber laws were used in 36 cases.

image.alt: The closed entry gate of the National Press Club in Dhaka
image.credit: Md Joni Hossain / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
At least 111 people faced legal action, arrest, attacks or other reprisals for expressing their views between January and October 2026, the Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) said on Wednesday (18 November), The Daily Star reported. Ijajul Islam, executive director of HRSS, presented the findings at a roundtable at the Jatiya Press Club.

Of the 111, 62 people (55.9%) were targeted for criticising the Prime Minister, his family, the government or BNP leaders. HRSS recorded 86 incidents in 38 districts. Sixty-six people were arrested or detained: 47 were shown arrested in cases and 19 were held without a case.

Of 66 legal actions, 36 were under cyber laws, 13 were for defamation or under the Penal Code, and 10 were under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Of the 84 people whose professions could be identified, 25 were journalists; cases were filed against 23 and four were arrested. Two people were beaten to death, and eight lost jobs or places in education.

HRSS also warned that the proposed amendments to the cyber protection law could restrict expression, privacy and journalism.

Why it matters

Civic space shapes what NGOs, researchers and community groups can safely say. The figures arrive while the government's revised cyber law draft is open for public comment.

What to watch

Whether the final cyber law draft narrows the offences HRSS flags, and whether rights groups and NGO networks send joint comments before the deadline.

Sources
